```{r}

library(tidyverse)

library(maps)

library(glue)
library(leaflet)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

#reads in a dataset holding information on marriage rates
marriage <- read.csv("C:/Users/cef22/OneDrive/Desktop/Claire2227.github.io/Marriage Rates by State_dfe_2019 2024.csv")

marriage
```

```{r}
#| include: false

#provides an outline of the US with state boundaries
us_states <- map_data("state")
head(us_states)
```

## Static Plot of Marriage Rates

This plot displays the marriage rate per 1,000 people for each state in the contiguous US during the year 2024. Marriages are counted in the state where the couple is married, not where the couple lives. Most states have marriage rates between 5 and 10. However, Nevada has a marriage rate of 24.8, reflecting the fact that Las Vegas is a popular destination to get married. Utah has the second highest marriage rate at 13.4


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: Static plot of the marriage rate per 1,000 people for each state in the contiguous US during the year 2024.

#filters the marriage dataset to only include data from the year 2024 and makes the state names lowercase
marriage <- marriage |>
  filter(YEAR == 2024) |>
  mutate(Location = str_to_lower(Location))

#joins the marriage dataset with the us_states dataset by their respective names for states
#creates a map of the states with states fill color corresponding to their marriage rates
marriage |>
  right_join(us_states, by = c("Location" = "region")) |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group)) + 
    geom_polygon(aes(fill = Marriage.rate), color = "black") + 
    labs(fill = "Marriage Rate per 1,000 People") +
    coord_map() +
    theme_void() +
    scale_fill_viridis()
```


```{r}
#| include: false

#reads in a dataset holding information on divorce rates
divorce <- read.csv("C:/Users/cef22/OneDrive/Desktop/Claire2227.github.io/Divorce Rates by State_dfe_2019 2024.csv")

divorce
```

## Static Plot of Divorce Rates

This plot displays states with a divorce rate of either above or below 2.5 per 1,000 people during the year 2024. Again, a divorce is counted in the state the marriage is legally ended. A majority of states have a divorce rate less than 2.5. However, the states with a divorce rate higher than 2.5 tend to be clustered in the south and west in a sort of diagonal line across the country. Additionally, some states have NA values where no divorce rate was found.


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: Static plot of states in the contiguous US with divorce rates above and below 2.5 per 1,000 people during the year 2024.

#filters the divorce dataset to only include data from the year 2024 and makes the state names lowercase
#creates two groups for the divorce dataset, one for states with a divorce rate greater than 2.5 and one for states with a divorce rate less than 2.5
divorce <- divorce |>
  filter(YEAR == 2024) |>
  mutate(Location = str_to_lower(Location),
         divorce_group = if_else(Divorce.rate > 2.5, 
                                 "Above 2.5", 
                                 "Less than 2.5"))


#joins the divorce dataset with the us_states dataset by their respective names for states
#creates a map of the states with states fill color corresponding to either above or below a marriage rate of 2.5
divorce |>
  right_join(us_states, by = c("Location" = "region")) |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group)) + 
  geom_polygon(
    aes(fill = divorce_group), 
    color = "darkgrey", 
    linewidth = 0.2
  ) + 
    labs(fill = "Divorce Rate Greater or Less Than 2.5 per 1,000 People") +
    coord_map() + 
    theme_void() +  
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("green", "pink"))
```

## Interactive Plot of Marriage Rates

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: Interactive plot of the marriage rate per 1,000 people for each state in the contiguous US during the year 2024.

#reads in an sf object containing geographic data on the US states
states_sf <- 
  read_sf(
    "https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/json/us-states.geojson"
  ) |>
  select(name, geometry)
#states_sf

#changes all the state names to lowercase
states_sf <- states_sf |>
  mutate(name = str_to_lower(name))

#joins the marriage and states dataset by their respective name for their state column
marriage_sf <- states_sf |>
  left_join(marriage, by = c("name" = "Location")) |>
  filter(!(name %in% c("alaska", "hawaii")))

#creates intervals for the labels on the plot
bins <- c(0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, Inf)
pal <- colorBin("YlOrRd", domain = marriage_sf$Marriage.rate, bins = bins)

#creates labels for each state that display the state name and marriage rate
marriage_sf <- marriage_sf |>
  mutate(labels = str_c(name, ": ", Marriage.rate, "  per 1,000 people"))

labels <- lapply(marriage_sf$labels, HTML)

#creates an interactive plot of the US states with fill color for each state corresponding to its marriage rate and applying the labels created above
leaflet(marriage_sf) |>
  setView(-96, 37.8, 4) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(Marriage.rate),
    weight = 2,
    opacity = 1,
    color = "white",
    dashArray = "3",
    fillOpacity = 0.7,
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 5,
      color = "#666",
      dashArray = "",
      fillOpacity = 0.7,
      bringToFront = TRUE),
    label = labels,
    labelOptions = labelOptions(
      style = list("font-weight" = "normal", padding = "3px 8px"),
      textsize = "15px",
      direction = "auto")) |>
  addLegend(pal = pal, values = ~Marriage.rate, opacity = 0.7, title = "Marriage Rate",
    position = "bottomright")
```

## Interactive Plot of Divorce Rates


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: Interactive plot of states in the contiguous US with divorce rates above and below 2.5 per 1,000 people during the year 2024.

#reads in an sf object containing geographic data on the US states
states_sf <- 
  read_sf(
    "https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/json/us-states.geojson"
  ) |>
  select(name, geometry)
#states_sf

#changes all the state names to lowercase
states_sf <- states_sf |>
  mutate(name = str_to_lower(name))

#joins the divorce and states dataset by their respective name for their state column
divorce_sf <- states_sf |>
  left_join(divorce, by = c("name" = "Location")) |>
  filter(!(name %in% c("alaska", "hawaii")))

#creates labels for each state that display the state name and if their divorce rate is above or below 2.5
divorce_sf <- divorce_sf |>
  mutate(labels = str_c(name, ": ", if_else(Divorce.rate > 2.5, 
                                 "Above 2.5 per 1,000 People", 
                                 "Less than 2.5 per 1,000 People")))

labels <- lapply(divorce_sf$labels, HTML)

#assigns the two groups in divorce group to a different color
levels(divorce_sf$divorce_group)
factpal <- colorFactor(
  palette = c("green", "pink"),
  domain = divorce_sf$divorce_group,
  levels = levels(divorce_sf$divorce_group))


#creates an interactive plot of the US states with fill color based on if the state has a divorce rate above or below 2.5 and applies the labels created above
leaflet(divorce_sf) |>
  setView(-96, 37.8, 4) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~factpal(divorce_group),
    weight = 2,
    opacity = 1,
    color = "white",
    dashArray = "3",
    fillOpacity = 0.7,
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 5,
      color = "#666",
      dashArray = "",
      fillOpacity = 0.7,
      bringToFront = TRUE),
    label = labels,
    labelOptions = labelOptions(
      style = list("font-weight" = "normal", padding = "3px 8px"),
      textsize = "15px",
      direction = "auto")) |>
  addLegend(pal = factpal, values = ~divorce_group, opacity = 0.7, title = "Divorce Rate",
    position = "bottomright")
```
